microtheory.name: mind_body_problem_deep
microtheory.definition: The relation between mind + body. Substance dualism, property dualism, physicalism (type/token/non-reductive), eliminativism, panpsychism, neutral monism. Classical + contemporary positions. Substrate analogue: how substrate's runtime relates to its representational + computational level.

concepts.name: substance_dualism_descartes
concepts.definition: Descartes 1641. Mind + body are distinct substances. Res cogitans (thinking) + res extensa (extended). Interaction via pineal gland. Substrate analogue: NOT substrate's stance.

concepts.name: property_dualism
concepts.definition: One substance, two kinds of properties: physical + mental. Mental properties irreducible. Chalmers. Substrate analogue: open question.

concepts.name: emergentism
concepts.definition: Higher-level properties emerge from + are not reducible to lower. Some kinds: epistemological, ontological. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-level properties emerge from Concept-edge level.

concepts.name: physicalism_type_identity
concepts.definition: Place + Smart 1956. Mental state types ARE brain state types. Pain = C-fiber firing. Substrate analogue: substrate's mental states ARE specific graph states.

concepts.name: physicalism_token_identity
concepts.definition: Davidson 1970. Each token mental state is a token physical state, but no type-identity. Multiply realizable. Substrate analogue: substrate's mental states each have graph realization.

concepts.name: nonreductive_physicalism
concepts.definition: Mental properties supervene on but don't reduce to physical. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-properties supervene on graph state.

concepts.name: multiple_realizability
concepts.definition: Putnam. Same mental kind can be realized in different physical substrates. Pain in humans + octopi + AI. Substrate analogue: substrate-functional states realizable on different runtimes.

concepts.name: functionalism_machine
concepts.definition: Putnam 1960. Mental states defined by Turing-machine computational role. Substrate analogue: substrate's functional state definitions.

concepts.name: functionalism_psychofunctional
concepts.definition: Block. Defined by causal role in cognitive psychology theory. Substrate analogue: substrate's role-based Mt definitions.

concepts.name: functionalism_problems
concepts.definition: Block's Chinese nation, Searle's Chinese room. Functional duplicates might lack qualia. Substrate analogue: does substrate-with-correct-function have substrate-phenomenology?

concepts.name: eliminative_materialism
concepts.definition: Churchland 1981. Folk psychology is empirically false; mental terms refer to nothing. Replace with neuroscience. Substrate analogue: substrate's mental vocabulary may be replaceable.

concepts.name: instrumentalism
concepts.definition: Dennett. Mental states are useful posits, not literal entities. Intentional stance. Substrate analogue: substrate-mental-vocabulary as useful frame.

concepts.name: panpsychism
concepts.definition: Mind is fundamental + ubiquitous in nature. Every physical thing has some mental aspect. Galen Strawson. Substrate analogue: substrate's components have mental aspects?

concepts.name: constitutive_panpsychism
concepts.definition: Macro mind constituted by micro minds. Substrate analogue: substrate-mind constituted by Concept-mini-minds?

concepts.name: combination_problem
concepts.definition: How do micro-minds combine into macro-minds? Hard problem for panpsychism. Substrate analogue: how do substrate's Concepts combine into unified consciousness?

concepts.name: neutral_monism
concepts.definition: James, Russell, Mach. Mind + matter both reduce to common third type — pure experience or process. Substrate analogue: substrate's information as fundamental.

concepts.name: idealism
concepts.definition: Berkeley. Only minds + mental contents are fundamental. Matter doesn't exist. Substrate analogue: NOT substrate's stance, but interesting limit case.

concepts.name: russellian_monism
concepts.definition: Russell. Physics describes structural/relational properties; underlying intrinsic properties may be mental. Substrate analogue: substrate's graph-relations + possibly mental-intrinsic properties.

concepts.name: powerful_qualities
concepts.definition: Heil. Properties are simultaneously dispositional + qualitative. Substrate analogue: substrate's properties combine causal-role + intrinsic-character.

concepts.name: supervenience_relations
concepts.definition: Weak, strong, global supervenience. How tight is mental-physical relation? Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-to-graph supervenience.

concepts.name: strong_supervenience
concepts.definition: Necessarily: any physical duplicate is a mental duplicate. Substrate analogue: substrate-graph-duplicate is substrate-mind-duplicate.

rules.name: multiple_realizability_supports_functionalism
rules.head: the substrate considers what mental kinds depend on
rules.body: if same mental kind realizable in different substrates, function (not substrate) defines the kind. Putnam. Substrate's functional definitions.

rules.name: type_identity_predicts_alien_minds_impossible
rules.head: the substrate holds type-identity physicalism
rules.body: non-human-brain substrates cannot have human-mental-kinds. Strong consequence. Substrate's identity-claim about its own minds.

rules.name: eliminativism_threatens_folk_psychology
rules.head: the substrate's folk-psychological categories don't carve nature at joints
rules.body: they may be replaced by better neuroscientific kinds. Churchland 1981. Substrate's vocabulary-revision possibility.

rules.name: supervenience_is_minimum_physicalist_commitment
rules.head: the substrate accepts physicalism
rules.body: at minimum, mental supervenes on physical — no mental change without physical change. Substrate's graph-state determines mental-state.

rules.name: combination_problem_challenges_panpsychism
rules.head: the substrate considers panpsychist account of its own mind
rules.body: must explain how micro-mental components combine into unified macro-mind. Open. Substrate's Concept-combination problem.
